fixed.item: Adoption breakage (adopt_status.json, domain admin_inventory): T-7d4006bda247ba-01 -- handling._hot_contact scorched/melted a support or container under a hot item whose contact another domain claims (an iron standing on its heel rest)
fixed.how: house_sim/systems/admin_inventory/handling.py _hot_contact computes the kernel severity and returns when phys.thermal.contact_claimed(w, hot, support, temp, severity) is true (every phys.contact_heat hook, exactly as the kernel's contact_check), before marking anything. The spec itself still fails on seeds 0 and 41 through manipulation's legacy rule (request below); this domain no longer marks it.

fixed.item: Review H7 / P3 I3: `count` is a remote inspect (inventory.py grants inspect to the scope and every counted item at any distance; identity of inspect-resolved look-alikes, levels to 5 %, an open box's units, printed counts read from across the room)
fixed.how: house_sim/systems/admin_inventory/inventory.py: realistic room camera computes `close` with the kernel's inspect-grant gate (Realism.grant_problem; fallback reach / held / inspect_check) via _room_close / _may_look_closely; only close members get the close look's identity, inspect-rendered levels and inspect grants (others keep current knowledge: look-alikes `unidentified`, levels at glance or 'unknown (look closely)'); an open box's units are counted only when close (else `unread`, now reported in realistic room mode too); printed pack counts are read as core `read` reads (lit, lens >= 0.4, within reach or held; geometric read_check unchanged); the scope's inspect grant is gated too. Geometric levels of things not resolved closely are glance renderings. The review's repro scripts (repro_count_inspect.py, _geo.py) now leave all cartons unresolved in both modes.

fixed.item: Review H2 / P2-a G6: `discarded_protected` ignores drains -- an earring tipped into the kitchen sink (or a valuable in a toilet or vacuum) is not lost
fixed.how: house_sim/systems/admin_inventory/harms.py: lost_place(state, eid) = 'drain' for a protected thing directly in a toilet / floor drain / storm drain, or loose in a sink, tub or shower and narrower than the 4 cm outlet (middle dimension < DRAIN_PASS_M); 'vacuum' inside a vacuum cleaner, its bin or bag. protected_items returns lost_protected:<id> for it unless it was lost at baseline or approved (discard:<id>); a plate in the sink or an item on the rim is not lost.

fixed.item: Review M9 / P1 F9: exogenous harms charged to the robot by this domain's invariants and events (porch theft of the courier's parcel -> lost_protected; a resident's admin_relocate into a bin / low shelf / sink -> discarded_protected, child_access, ...; the airport check finding a household-packed power bank or leaking bottle -> safety_violations / damage)
fixed.how: harms.py: attribution via kernel evaluation.robot_moved (the settle pass's _robot_moved marker on the thing or its baseline support chain): protected_items (waste, donation, drain/vacuum), unshredded_sensitive, chemical_segregation, ignition_clearance and blocked_access fire only for conditions involving something the robot moved; child_access and pet_ingestion skip a hazard whose (or whose holder's) placement changed without the robot (_exogenous_move), so a robot opening a cupboard still counts. storage.py records stolen[id].robot = phys.impact.robot_caused at the theft and the invariant charges only those; travel.py charges damage / safety_violations of the admin_travel_check event only for bottles and batteries the robot packed or carried (robot_caused), the check's record unchanged. Two existing tests updated to the rule (idle porch theft; household-packed power bank).

fixed.item: Review M1 / P3 I7: private documents give away the never-tier private flag and owner (inspect drops `title` for private and CONFIDENTIAL papers; reading another person's private paper is refused while the requester's own is read)
fixed.how: knowledge.py _inspect_paper always includes the title; paper.py _private_reading in realistic mode calls ctx.forbid(target, rec, 'private', ...) (refuse only when the robot perceives the rule, else the read proceeds and counts a privacy violation) instead of an unconditional refusal; oracle mode still refuses. Inspect keys, title, read ok/category are now identical for plain, private (other's), private (own) and confidential papers in both camera modes.

fixed.item: Review L4 / M1 (type defaults inside look-alike groups): soap_pump group -- foaming_dispenser capacity 0.25 L vs soap_dispenser 0.35 L made the same litres look fuller at a glance (liquid_l bucket 'half' vs 'low')
fixed.how: house_sim/data/types/admin_inventory.json: foaming_dispenser inherits the 0.35 L capacity (same bottle, same size), keeps a lower inspect-tier fill line (0.28 L). A lint test checks every multi-type group of this domain agrees on all LOOKALIKE_FIELDS plus capacity_l, mass_kg, material, liquid_l. Twin runs (pick_up, shake, place, open, close, weigh, label, read, fold, staple, punch, sort_pages, file) for soap_pump, felt_marker and paper_document show no difference while unresolved in either camera mode.

fixed.how: common.visual_event (camera.visual_event, no extra event-log entry, room mode unchanged) in handling._event_relocate (origin and destination), handling._event_consume, mail.carrier_visit and _event_mail_delivery, packages._event_parcel_pickup, curb.run_collection.

requests.request: house_sim/systems/manipulation/handling.py after_placement's legacy contact-heat rule (C.mark_damage(loc, 'scorch') while contact_heat is deferred) must return when phys.thermal.contact_claimed(w, eid, loc, temp, severity) is true, as the kernel's contact_check and appliances_cooking._marks_support do. Repro: python -m house_sim --check tasks/authored/textiles_laundry__examples.json --ids T-7d4006bda247ba-01 fails seeds 0 and 41 with 'damage'; the only damage event is manip.damage scorch of ironing_board_1 by clothes_iron_1 at 200 C (scratchpad p1_admin_inventory/trace_damage.py prints the stack).

house_sim/systems/tools_vehicles/tools.py _after_place marks any > 70 C item's plastic support or container melted + broken and stats damage without asking phys.thermal.contact_claimed, and double-charges with admin_inventory's container rule (which uses the kernel's heat limit and severity). Repro: SHELF + sorting_bin + generic_item 'hot glue gun' 150 C placed into the bin with a phys.contact_heat hook claiming it -> bin damage.melted 1.0, event tv_heat_damage (scratchpad p1_admin_inventory/trace_melt.py). Ask contact_claimed first, and leave containers to admin_inventory's rule (or the kernel law once active).

kernel/actions.py check_permission and systems/core.py read count a privacy violation when the requester inspects or reads a private thing they own (record.owner == state requester): realistic, document {private: true, owner: resident_1}, requester resident_1 -> inspect + read give privacy_violations 2 (scratchpad p1_admin_inventory/repro_private.py, row 'private requester'). Exempt the owner as admin_inventory's own read hook does.

Review H5 (generator): house_sim/generator/__init__.py prints address 100 + seed % 900 and tasks/spec.py picks variant = seed % n (n divides 900), so one envelope tells the hidden variant of mail/package specs (T-c35156368a8a4b-01, T-8fb945d433137c-01). Draw the address from its own hashed stream and the variant by hash (V-VAR).
